steps.title: Isolate the affected system
steps.plain: Disconnect the affected computer from the network to stop active encryption and limit spread. Keep the system powered on unless directed otherwise so evidence can be preserved.
steps.linux:
sudo iptables -I INPUT -j DROP
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -j DROP
steps.windows: netsh advfirewall set allprofiles firewallpolicy blockinbound,blockoutbound
steps.exp: The affected system can no longer communicate with the network.

steps.title: Identify the ransomware activity
steps.plain: Identify the suspicious process, executable, file extensions, and network connections associated with the ransomware. Record process IDs and external addresses.
steps.windows:
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select -First 20
netstat -ano
steps.exp: You have identified the suspicious process and relevant network indicators.

steps.title: Preserve evidence
steps.plain: Capture logs, process information, network information, screenshots, and suspicious file details before removing the malware.
steps.windows:
Get-EventLog -LogName Security -Newest 500 | Export-Csv events.csv
ipconfig /all > network_info.txt
steps.exp: Evidence is stored and can be attached to the incident case.

steps.title: Stop the malicious process
steps.plain: Terminate the confirmed ransomware process after evidence has been preserved. This stops ongoing encryption activity.
steps.windows: Stop-Process -Id [PID] -Force
steps.exp: The ransomware process is no longer running and active encryption has stopped.

steps.title: Block the attacker connection
steps.plain: Block identified command-and-control or malicious external addresses so the attacker cannot reconnect to the affected system.
steps.windows: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Block Ransomware C2" -Direction Outbound -RemoteAddress [ATTACKER_IP] -Action Block
steps.exp: The identified malicious connection is blocked.

steps.title: Recover and verify
steps.plain: Restore affected files or systems from a known-clean backup. Verify important files and confirm the system is operating normally before reconnecting it.
steps.windows: wbadmin start recovery -version:[BACKUP_VERSION]
steps.exp: Clean data is restored and the recovered system passes basic verification.

steps.title: Confirm clean state and close
steps.plain: Confirm the ransomware activity has stopped, required systems are stable, and the response record is complete before closing the incident.
steps.linux: # Verify services, logs, and restored files before reconnecting the host
steps.windows: # Verify services, logs, and restored files before reconnecting the host
steps.exp: The environment is stable, recovery is verified, and the incident is ready to close.

steps.title: Block the attacking source
steps.plain: Block the source address responsible for the repeated authentication attempts.
steps.windows: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Block Brute Force Source" -Direction Inbound -RemoteAddress [ATTACKER_IP] -Action Block
steps.exp: Further authentication attempts from the identified source are blocked.

steps.title: Protect targeted accounts
steps.plain: Lock accounts receiving excessive failed login attempts so compromised credentials cannot be used while the investigation continues.
steps.windows: Disable-ADAccount -Identity [username]
steps.exp: Targeted accounts are protected from further access.

steps.title: Review authentication logs
steps.plain: Determine which accounts were targeted and whether any successful login occurred during the attack window.
steps.windows: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName="Security";Id=4624,4625} -MaxEvents 100
steps.exp: You know which accounts were targeted and whether successful authentication occurred.

steps.title: Reset affected credentials
steps.plain: Reset credentials for accounts that were targeted or successfully accessed. Use approved strong-password requirements.
steps.windows: Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity [username] -Reset
steps.exp: Affected accounts have new credentials.

steps.title: Strengthen authentication controls
steps.plain: Review lockout and authentication controls to reduce the chance of repeated password-guessing attacks.
steps.windows: Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutDuration 00:30:00
steps.exp: The environment has stronger controls against repeated authentication attempts.

steps.title: Document and close
steps.plain: Record the attack source, affected accounts, successful logins, actions taken, and final outcome.
steps.linux: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.windows: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.exp: The incident has a complete response record.

steps.title: Verify and close the case
steps.plain: Confirm that repeated authentication attempts have stopped, affected accounts are secure, and the response record is complete.
steps.linux: # Review recent authentication events and confirm no continued attack
steps.windows: # Review recent Security events and confirm no continued attack
steps.exp: No continued brute force activity is observed and the case is ready to close.

steps.title: Identify the account and command
steps.plain: Confirm which account performed the unexpected administrative action and record the command, timestamp, and affected system.
steps.windows: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName="Security";Id=4688} -MaxEvents 100
steps.exp: The account, command, time, and system are identified.

steps.title: Preserve relevant evidence
steps.plain: Save authentication, process, and system logs before changing the account or removing activity.
steps.windows: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -MaxEvents 500 | Export-Csv security_events.csv
steps.exp: Relevant evidence is preserved for investigation.

steps.title: Restrict suspicious access
steps.plain: Temporarily remove elevated access or lock the account if the activity is not authorised.
steps.windows: Disable-ADAccount -Identity [username]
steps.exp: The suspicious account can no longer perform additional privileged actions.

steps.title: Check for persistence
steps.plain: Look for newly created administrator accounts, scheduled tasks, services, startup entries, or other mechanisms that could preserve attacker access.
steps.windows:
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators
Get-ScheduledTask
steps.exp: No unauthorised persistence remains, or suspicious persistence is documented.

steps.title: Restore approved privileges
steps.plain: Remove unauthorised privilege changes and restore the account to its approved role after the investigation.
steps.linux: # Remove unauthorised group membership and restore approved access
steps.windows: # Remove unauthorised group membership and restore approved access
steps.exp: The account has only its approved permissions.

steps.title: Document and close
steps.plain: Record the escalation path, evidence, containment actions, and final determination.
steps.linux: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.windows: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.exp: The privilege escalation incident is fully documented.

steps.title: Verify and close the case
steps.plain: Confirm that elevated access is restored only where approved, no persistence remains, and the incident record is complete.
steps.linux: # Verify approved privileges and review recent account activity
steps.windows: # Verify approved privileges and review recent account activity
steps.exp: Approved access is confirmed and the case is ready to close.

steps.title: Identify the changed files
steps.plain: Review the file integrity alert and identify exactly which protected files changed, when they changed, and on which system.
steps.windows: Get-Item [FILE] | Format-List *
steps.exp: The changed files and timestamps are identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence
steps.plain: Capture the current file state, relevant logs, and the account or process responsible for the change.
steps.windows:
Get-FileHash [FILE] -Algorithm SHA256 | Out-File file_hash.txt
Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -MaxEvents 200 | Export-Csv security_events.csv
steps.exp: The original change and supporting evidence are recorded.

steps.title: Determine whether the change was authorised
steps.plain: Compare the change with approved maintenance, deployment, configuration management, or administrator activity.
steps.linux: # Compare timestamps with approved maintenance records
steps.windows: # Compare timestamps with approved maintenance records
steps.exp: The change is classified as authorised or suspicious.

steps.title: Contain suspicious activity
steps.plain: If the change is unauthorised, restrict the responsible account or process and investigate related activity on the system.
steps.windows: Disable-ADAccount -Identity [username]
steps.exp: Further unauthorised changes are prevented while investigation continues.

steps.title: Restore the approved file state
steps.plain: Restore the affected configuration or system file from a known-good source after confirming the correct version.
steps.windows: # Restore the approved file version from your configuration backup
steps.exp: The protected file matches the approved configuration.

steps.title: Document and close
steps.plain: Record the changed files, authorisation decision, evidence, corrective action, and final outcome.
steps.linux: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.windows: # Complete incident notes and close when verified
steps.exp: The file integrity incident is fully documented.

steps.title: Verify system stability and close
steps.plain: Monitor the protected files and system activity after restoration to confirm that no unexpected changes recur.
steps.linux: # Verify file hashes and monitor for additional unexpected changes
steps.windows: # Verify file hashes and monitor for additional unexpected changes
steps.exp: The approved file state remains stable and the case is ready to close.
